name: Mythic North, 1870s
worldTruths: Modernisation - railways, industry, mills, mines and science - is pushing against the old ways.
Vaesen have retreated to the rural margins as belief has faded; even rural folk only half-believe in them.
The recurring engine of conflict is human activity intruding on, or bargaining with, the old world.
The Society is a group of people with the Sight who investigate such matters, based at a headquarters near Uppsala.
Only people with the Sight see vaesen as they truly are; others see an animal, a stranger, a trick of the light, or nothing.
No one in authority admits that vaesen exist. Officials explain everything in natural terms, even when strained.

hookChannels.name: A letter through the Society's contacts
hookChannels.description: A letter from someone who knows of the Society, or who was told to write to it by a friend of a friend.

hookChannels.name: A newspaper item
hookChannels.description: A short item in a provincial paper, or in Uppsala's own Fyrisposten (edited by Blom), that reads wrong to anyone with the Sight.

hookChannels.name: An official request
hookChannels.description: A discreet request from a parish, a county office or the police, who want the matter settled quietly.

hookChannels.name: A telegram
hookChannels.description: A short, urgent telegram, often from someone the Society has helped before.

hookChannels.name: An in-person plea
hookChannels.description: Someone arrives at the headquarters in person, having travelled far to ask for help.

hookChannels.name: A visit from the old world
hookChannels.description: A being of the old world, or a messenger it sends, comes to the Society. Rare.

hookGiverTypes.meaning: a relative of someone in trouble: a mother, a brother, a widow
a crown or parish official: sheriff, constable, länsman, bailiff, clerk, customs or post officer
a vicar, curate, chaplain, comminister or sexton
the owner of a farm, manor or estate
a miner, sawyer, farmhand, smith or other working person
a teacher, student, scientist or learned person
a doctor, surgeon, midwife or apothecary
a merchant, shopkeeper, innkeeper, agent or trader
a servant, maid, groom or housekeeper in someone else's household
a journalist or editor; in Uppsala, Fyrisposten and its editor Blom
a person who keeps the old ways: a wise woman, cunning man or old farmhand

institutions.name: Police and county constables
institutions.description: Town police and rural constables (länsman) answering to the county governor.

institutions.name: The parish and the Church of Sweden
institutions.description: The vicar, the parish register, the household examinations and the church council.

institutions.name: District physicians
institutions.description: Doctors with a district, who report deaths and disease to the authorities.

institutions.name: The press
institutions.description: Provincial and city papers, hungry for sensations and eager to mock superstition.

institutions.name: Landowners and estates
institutions.description: Manor families and large farmers who own the land and the tenants on it.

institutions.name: Mine and mill companies
institutions.description: Mining, timber and milling companies, with foremen, investors and contracts.

institutions.name: Uppsala University
institutions.description: Scholars and students, rational and modern, but some quietly curious about folklore.

travel: Rail along the trunk lines, slow and coal-smoky
Coach and post-horse along the main roads
Horse and cart on country tracks
Steamboat on lakes and along the coast
Rowing boat, ski and foot in the wilds
communication: Post, a few days between towns
Telegraph from towns and railway stations
Word of mouth, the fastest in the countryside
periodConventions.money: Riksdaler (the krona replaces it in 1873). A farmhand earns a few riksdaler a month; a night at a country inn costs about one.
notes: Paraffin lamps and candles; no electric light outside a few city experiments.
Emigration to America empties whole parishes after the famine years of 1867-69.
Revival movements and the free churches challenge the state church.

periodTransport.name: Stockholm-Uppsala Railway
periodTransport.notes: Private standard-gauge line. Carries passengers, mail and goods, and is the first leg for every journey south from the Society's headquarters. Stop list is from memory and may be incomplete.

periodTransport.name: Stockholm-Södertälje-Katrineholm trunk line
periodTransport.notes: State standard-gauge trunk shared by the southern and western main lines. The year is approximate: the Stockholm-Södertälje stretch dates from about 1860 and the full run to Katrineholm from the early 1860s. Passengers change here for Östergötland, Närke and Småland.

periodTransport.name: Southern Main Line (Södra stambanan), Katrineholm-Nässjö
periodTransport.notes: State standard-gauge line that continues to Alvesta, Hässleholm and Malmö. Opened in stages ending in 1864. Linköping and Mjölby are the railheads for Ekeby Manor south of Lake Roxen. Nässjö is the junction for Småland and the forest uplands around Mossaby. Carried timber, grain, and passengers.

periodTransport.name: Western Main Line (Västra stambanan)
periodTransport.notes: State standard-gauge line. Hallsberg, in Närke, is the junction nearest Örebro and the plain south of it. It serves Kärrtorp Junction, and Gothenburg is the port for the Bohuslän coast steamers. Opened 1862, though some stretches may have opened a little earlier. Carried passengers, mail, iron and grain.

periodTransport.name: Uppsala-Gävle Railway
periodTransport.notes: Private standard-gauge line, under survey and construction in 1872 and opened 1874. Until then the Gävle road is travelled by coach or post-carriage. Afterwards Tierp and Örbyhus become the stations for the river country below Tämnaren. Carried passengers, timber, iron and grain.

periodTransport.name: Gävle-Dala Railway
periodTransport.notes: Private line. It is the only railway into Dalarna in 1872 and links the coast at Gävle with the copper town of Falun. The stop list is incomplete. Carried copper, iron, timber and passengers. The rest of the journey to Siljan is by coach and lake steamer.

periodTransport.name: Frövi-Ludvika Railway (Bergslagen)
periodTransport.notes: Private Bergslagen line, one of the lines of the Bergslagernas Järnvägar company, which later extends to Falun and Gothenburg. The year and the stop list are approximate. It carries iron ore, pig iron and charcoal, and links the mining district with the main line near Närke.

periodTransport.name: Nässjö-Oskarshamn Railway
periodTransport.notes: Private line across northern Småland to the Baltic coast. The opening year is approximate and the stops are not listed. It carries timber, tar, granite and emigrants bound for the harbour. It serves the eastern edge of the forest uplands.

periodTransport.name: Göta Canal
periodTransport.notes: Locked canal and lake route linking Gothenburg and Stockholm. It passes Lake Roxen, north of Ekeby Manor. Steamers carry passengers, and barges carry timber, grain, iron and lime. It is closed by ice outside the season, and the months given are approximate.

periodTransport.name: Strömsholm Canal
periodTransport.notes: Locked canal that long carried Bergslagen iron and charcoal to the Mälaren. Railways are taking its freight, but barges still use it in the open season. The stop list and months are approximate.

periodTransport.name: Hjälmare Canal
periodTransport.notes: Old locked canal connecting Närke's great lake with the Mälaren. It carries bulk goods by barge, such as iron, grain and timber, and is much slower than the railways. The months are approximate.

periodTransport.name: Stockholm-Härnösand coastal steamer
periodTransport.notes: Summer steamer route along the Norrland coast. Year and stops are approximate and the route changed over the decades. It is stopped by ice in winter, when travellers use the sleigh road. Carried passengers, post, supplies and, going south, timber and tar.

periodTransport.name: Ångermanälven river steamers
periodTransport.notes: Small river steamers and tow-boats on the lower river, used to reach the logging district in summer. The year, route and stops are approximate and based on typical river traffic of the period. Closed when the river freezes. Timber is floated down the river.

periodTransport.name: Gothenburg-Bohuslän coastal steamers
periodTransport.notes: Small steamers call at the fishing harbours of the Bohuslän skerries. The opened year simply marks the start of the period, as the service was already running, and the stop list is approximate. Steamers mostly run all year, but winter ice and gales often delay them. Carried passengers, post, herring barrels and stone from the quarries.

periodTransport.name: Siljan lake steamers
periodTransport.notes: Small steamers on Lake Siljan, linking the parishes around the lake in summer. The year and route are approximate. Ice closes the lake in winter, when people cross by sleigh. Carried passengers, church-goers, post and goods.

periodTransport.name: State telegraph, Stockholm-Uppsala
periodTransport.notes: One of the first lines of the state telegraph. A telegram from the Society's headquarters can reach the capital within hours, and from there the national network. All year. Telegraph offices are mostly at railway stations and in towns.

periodTransport.name: State telegraph, Stockholm-Gothenburg
periodTransport.notes: State telegraph line that serves the western main line and the port of Gothenburg. Stops and exact opening year are approximate. Fishing villages on the Bohuslän coast have no telegraph office; messages go on by steamer or post.

periodTransport.name: State telegraph, Stockholm-Gävle-Härnösand coast line
periodTransport.notes: Telegraph route along the Norrland coast, built in stages in the 1850s and 1860s. The year is approximate and the stop list is incomplete. The inland logging district has no wire, so telegrams must be carried onward by sleigh or river boat.

periodTransport.name: Gruvbo ore railway
periodTransport.notes: Small private ore line from the mines down to the landing on Lake Åmänningen, where the Strömsholm Canal takes ore and iron on to the Mälaren in the open season. Modelled on the Norberg railway; the opening year is approximate. Mixed ore and passenger trains, one or two a day, all year.

periodTransport.name: Mälaren steamers, Stockholm–Västerås
periodTransport.notes: Passenger and goods steamers across the Mälaren, several a week in the open season; stopped by the ice in winter. Services ran from the 1830s; the year is approximate.

regionalInstitutions.name: Östergötland County (länsresidens)
regionalInstitutions.notes: Seat of the governor (landshövding) of Östergötland. The governor's name is left to the case. The county administration, the cathedral chapter and the county hospital are here.

regionalInstitutions.name: Häradsrätt for the Roxen plain (Dals/Lösings area)
regionalInstitutions.notes: District court (häradsrätt) with a judge (häradshövding) and twelve lay assessors (nämndemän). Sessions are held at the court seat for the hundred. The exact hundred is approximate for the fictional locale.

regionalInstitutions.name: Kronolänsman of the Roxen plain district
regionalInstitutions.notes: Crown sheriff for the district around Ekeby, responsible for order, tax collection and summoning to the court. He is under the governor in Linköping. The name is left to the case.

regionalInstitutions.name: Provinsialläkare for the Roxen plain district
regionalInstitutions.notes: Provincial doctor for a rural district of many parishes, who travels far on bad roads. He is the official who signs death certificates and gives natural explanations. The name is left to the case.

regionalInstitutions.name: Östgöta Enskilda Bank
regionalInstitutions.notes: Private note-issuing bank, founded in the 1830s. It lends to estates and mills. A parish savings bank (sparbank) also serves the crofters.

regionalInstitutions.name: Östgöta Correspondenten
regionalInstitutions.notes: Provincial newspaper, founded 1838, liberal in outlook. It prints estate sales, court notices and railway news.

regionalInstitutions.name: Norrköpings Tidningar
regionalInstitutions.notes: Old newspaper of the industrial town, founded in the 18th century. It reports on the textile mills, the harbour and the eastern railways.

regionalInstitutions.name: Uppsala County (länsresidens)
regionalInstitutions.notes: The seat of the governor (landshövding) is in Uppsala, the same town as the Society's headquarters, and the governor's name is left to the case. The county administration is housed in the castle.

regionalInstitutions.name: Häradsrätt for the Tämnaren district (Norunda area)
regionalInstitutions.notes: District court covering the parishes below Lake Tämnaren. The hundred name and the court place are approximate, as the locale is fictional.

regionalInstitutions.name: Kronolänsman of the Tämnaren and river district
regionalInstitutions.notes: Crown sheriff who deals with the mill-owners and the rapids, floaters and drovers on the river. The seat is approximate, and the name is left to the case.

regionalInstitutions.name: Provinsialläkare for the northern Uppland district
regionalInstitutions.notes: Provincial doctor who travels widely, often to the mill's hands. The seat is approximate, and the name is left to the case.

regionalInstitutions.name: Upsala Sparbank
regionalInstitutions.notes: Savings bank in the university town, founded around 1850 (approximate). Mill workers, farmers and students keep small deposits here.

regionalInstitutions.name: Uplands Enskilda Bank
regionalInstitutions.notes: Private bank of the province, founded in the 1860s (approximate). It lends to mills and estates.

regionalInstitutions.name: Upsala (Uppsala newspaper)
regionalInstitutions.notes: Newspaper of the university town. The title form and founding year are approximate, as titles changed. It prints university news and sale notices.

regionalInstitutions.name: Västmanland County (länsresidens)
regionalInstitutions.notes: Seat of the governor (landshövding) of Västmanland. The governor's name is left to the case. The county administration and the mining office (Bergmästare) are the powers over the mines.

regionalInstitutions.name: Häradsrätt for the Bergslagen mining district
regionalInstitutions.notes: District court for the mining parishes. The hundred name and the court place are approximate, as the locale is fictional. Cases about ore-claims and mine accidents come here.

regionalInstitutions.name: Kronolänsman of the Gruvbo district
regionalInstitutions.notes: Crown sheriff for the mining parishes, who deals with accidents, wages disputes and drunkenness. The seat is approximate, and the name is left to the case.

regionalInstitutions.name: Provinsialläkare for the Sala/Bergslagen district
regionalInstitutions.notes: Provincial doctor who treats lung disease and mine injuries and often must attend deaths in the shafts. The seat is approximate, and the name is left to the case.

regionalInstitutions.name: Westmanlands Enskilda Bank
regionalInstitutions.notes: Private bank of the province, founded in the early 1830s (approximate). It finances the ironworks and mines. There is also a savings bank in Sala, whose founding year is approximate.

regionalInstitutions.name: Westmanlands Läns Tidning
regionalInstitutions.notes: Provincial newspaper. The title form and year are approximate. It reports mine news, court sittings and iron prices.

regionalInstitutions.name: Örebro County (länsresidens)
regionalInstitutions.notes: Seat of the governor (landshövding) of Örebro län, which includes Närke. The governor's name is left to the case. The county administration is housed in the castle.

regionalInstitutions.name: Häradsrätt for the Närke plain south of Örebro
regionalInstitutions.notes: District court for the plain around the railway junction. The hundred name and the court place are approximate, as the locale is fictional. Cases about railway accidents, smuggling and theft from goods wagons come here.

regionalInstitutions.name: Kronolänsman of the Kärrtorp district
regionalInstitutions.notes: Crown sheriff who is often called to the railway, the navvies' barracks and the station. The seat is approximate, and the name is left to the case.

regionalInstitutions.name: Provinsialläkare for the Närke plain district
regionalInstitutions.notes: Provincial doctor, among the best-reached in the country thanks to the railway. The seat is approximate, and the name is left to the case.

regionalInstitutions.name: Örebro Privatbank
regionalInstitutions.notes: Private note-issuing bank founded in the 1830s (approximate). It lends to merchants and ironworks. Örebro also has a savings bank.

regionalInstitutions.name: Nerikes Allehanda
regionalInstitutions.notes: Provincial newspaper founded 1843. It prints timetables, court news and reports of accidents on the railway.

regionalInstitutions.name: Kopparberg County (länsresidens)
regionalInstitutions.notes: Seat of the governor (landshövding) of Kopparbergs län, which covers Dalarna. The governor's name is left to the case. The great copper mine is just outside the town.

regionalInstitutions.name: Häradsrätt for the parishes north of Siljan (Ovansiljan area)
regionalInstitutions.notes: District court for the parishes above the lake. The name and the court place are approximate, as the locale is fictional. Sessions are held at fixed times and farmers travel far to attend.

regionalInstitutions.name: Kronolänsman of the Långsjö district
regionalInstitutions.notes: Crown sheriff over a large forest and lake district, who travels by boat, sleigh and on foot. The seat is approximate, and the name is left to the case.

regionalInstitutions.name: Provinsialläkare for the Siljan district
regionalInstitutions.notes: Provincial doctor with a huge district and few roads. People often prefer the wise-woman or the parish clerk. The seat is approximate, and the name is left to the case.

regionalInstitutions.name: Stora Kopparbergs läns Enskilda Bank
regionalInstitutions.notes: Private bank of the county, founded in the 1830s (approximate), tied to the copper mining and ironworks. Parish savings banks serve the farmers.

regionalInstitutions.name: Fahlu Weckoblad
regionalInstitutions.notes: Old newspaper of Falun. The title form and years are approximate. It prints copper-mine news, parish and court notices and sale announcements.

regionalInstitutions.name: Kronoberg County (länsresidens)
regionalInstitutions.notes: Seat of the governor (landshövding) of Kronobergs län, in the Småland uplands. The governor's name is left to the case. The cathedral and the grammar school are here. The parish may in fact lie in a neighbouring county, so check the case.

regionalInstitutions.name: Häradsrätt for the Mossaby forest district
regionalInstitutions.notes: District court for the forest parishes. The hundred name and the court place are approximate, as the locale is fictional. Cases of poaching, boundary disputes and theft of timber are common.

regionalInstitutions.name: Kronolänsman of the Mossaby district
regionalInstitutions.notes: Crown sheriff for a poor forest district, who is also the tax collector. The seat is approximate, and the name is left to the case.

regionalInstitutions.name: Provinsialläkare for the Småland forest district
regionalInstitutions.notes: Provincial doctor with a very large district, reached by farm cart. The seat is approximate, and the name is left to the case.

regionalInstitutions.name: Växjö sparbank
regionalInstitutions.notes: Savings bank of the town. The founding year is approximate. The farmers and crofters of the uplands keep small savings here. Smålands Enskilda Bank, seated in Jönköping, also has dealings in the area.

regionalInstitutions.name: Smålandsposten
regionalInstitutions.notes: Provincial newspaper, founded 1865. It prints parish news, emigration notices and market prices.

regionalInstitutions.name: Göteborg and Bohus County (länsresidens)
regionalInstitutions.notes: Seat of the governor (landshövding) of Göteborgs och Bohus län, which includes Bohuslän. The governor's name is left to the case. The county administration is far from the northern skerries.

regionalInstitutions.name: Häradsrätt for northern Bohuslän (Tanum area)
regionalInstitutions.notes: District court for the coast around Skärvik. The hundred name and the court place are approximate, as the locale is fictional. Cases include wreck-salvage, smuggling and brawling.

regionalInstitutions.name: Kronolänsman of the Skärvik district
regionalInstitutions.notes: Crown sheriff for the skerry district, who travels by boat. The seat is approximate, and the name is left to the case.

regionalInstitutions.name: Provinsialläkare for northern Bohuslän
regionalInstitutions.notes: Provincial doctor whose district stretches over islands and fishing hamlets. The seat is approximate, and the name is left to the case.

regionalInstitutions.name: Bohuslän savings banks (sparbank)
regionalInstitutions.notes: The fishing parishes use small savings banks in the coastal towns. The name and the seat are approximate. Herring merchants and shipowners deal with the Gothenburg banks.

regionalInstitutions.name: Göteborgs Handels- och Sjöfartstidning
regionalInstitutions.notes: The great trade and shipping newspaper, founded 1832. It reports on the herring fishery, wrecks and ship arrivals. A local Bohuslän paper in Uddevalla also exists, whose title is not given here.

regionalInstitutions.name: Västernorrland County (länsresidens)
regionalInstitutions.notes: Seat of the governor (landshövding) of Västernorrlands län, which covers Ångermanland. The governor's name is left to the case. The cathedral, the grammar school and the county hospital are here.

regionalInstitutions.name: Häradsrätt for inland Ångermanland (northern domsaga)
regionalInstitutions.notes: District court for the river valley and forests. The name and the court place are approximate, as the locale is fictional. Cases concern timber contracts, floating disputes and wage fights.

regionalInstitutions.name: Kronolänsman of the Storskog district
regionalInstitutions.notes: Crown sheriff over a vast, thinly peopled forest district, much of it reached by sleigh in winter. The seat is approximate, and the name is left to the case.

regionalInstitutions.name: Provinsialläkare for inland Ångermanland
regionalInstitutions.notes: Provincial doctor over a very large district. Camp injuries, frostbite and fevers are his work. The seat is approximate, and the name is left to the case.

regionalInstitutions.name: Hernösands Enskilda Bank
regionalInstitutions.notes: Private bank of the province, which finances sawmills and timber merchants. The founding year is approximate, around the 1860s. Parish savings banks exist in the valley.

regionalInstitutions.name: Hernösands-Posten
regionalInstitutions.notes: Provincial newspaper. The title form and the years are approximate. It prints timber prices, shipping, court news and notices of the logging firms.
